title: Paid social
purpose: When the Meta or TikTok numbers land on a Monday, before a launch, or when ads or stock start to run out, open Paid social to know what to cut, hold or scale so each ad dollar returns the most gross profit.
fires: the agency's Monday call and slide deck, the return-on-spend spreadsheet, the 11pm Ads Manager check, and the habit of waiting a week to see
not_for: a store spending under about $1,000 a month on social ads, or one with no purchase tracking yet, where a weekly look in Ads Manager is enough

jobs.job: When the weekly numbers land on Monday with spend up and revenue flat, tell me by noon which ad sets to cut, hold or scale and by how much, so I stop the week's budget leaking into losers
jobs.circumstance: Monday 9am, last week's numbers in, spend up 20 percent, store revenue flat, the media buyer waiting for a call before the team meeting

progress.functional: know which ad sets lose money, how much each costs us, and what to do with each today
progress.emotional: stop dreading Monday numbers; feel in control of the budget
progress.social: give the buyer a clear call and look decisive to a partner or client

jobs.hire_today: the agency's Monday call, a spreadsheet of last week's return, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the Monday call and the spreadsheet; the habit of waiting another week to see

forces.push: money leaves every day the decision waits
forces.pull: a ranked list of losers and winners with dollars at stake and one decision each
forces.habit: the agency has always made this call
forces.anxiety: what if I cut an ad set that was about to turn, or the numbers are wrong

jobs.little_hire: every Monday, and any day spend jumps 20 percent

watch.metric: share of spend in ad sets above the target cost per purchase after spending 3 times that target, 7 day click, trailing 7 days

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 35 percent of spend sits in ad sets above target. After: under 10 percent within 14 days, each cut and hold logged.
jobs.not_for: a store spending under $1,000 a month, where a weekly look in Ads Manager is enough

jobs.job: When Meta shows a great week but the bank balance and store orders do not agree, tell me what the ads really made before I raise the budget, so I do not scale on a number that is not real
jobs.circumstance: Tuesday, Meta says 4x return, store new-customer revenue says half that, the buyer wants to raise budget 30 percent

progress.functional: compare Meta's claimed sales with store orders and new customers for the same days
progress.emotional: stop the sick feeling that the ads look good only inside Meta
progress.social: back a budget decision with numbers a partner or investor will trust

jobs.hire_today: nothing, or the agency's word; checking by hand means exporting 2 reports and a spreadsheet nobody has time for
jobs.fire: trusting Meta's own return column; the agency's word

forces.push: a raise on a false number burns cash for weeks before anyone sees it
forces.pull: Meta's number and the store's number side by side, with the gap and what it means for the raise
forces.habit: Meta's number is the one everyone quotes
forces.anxiety: what if the store number is wrong too and I block a good raise

jobs.little_hire: before every budget raise, and monthly

watch.metric: gap between Meta-reported purchase value and store new-customer revenue on the same days, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager and store orders

drives.metric: new-customer revenue per ad dollar across all channels, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Meta claims $120,000 and the store shows $70,000 from new buyers. After: raises are judged on the store figure, and 2 of 3 planned raises are held.
jobs.not_for: a store with under 30 orders a month from ads, where the numbers are too small to compare

jobs.job: When I wake to spend doubled overnight or sales at zero, tell me the cause before 9am: tracking, a rejected ad, the site or the market, so I fix the right thing before the day is lost
jobs.circumstance: 7am, phone alert, yesterday's spend 2 times normal or purchases at 0, the buyer not online yet

progress.functional: find the cause of the jump and the ad sets behind it
progress.emotional: stop the panic of not knowing what broke
progress.social: be the one who found it, not the one who missed it

jobs.hire_today: the media buyer the next morning, or nothing until someone notices
jobs.fire: the next-day check and the guessing

forces.push: a broken pixel or a site outage can burn a day of budget
forces.pull: the jump traced to its cause, with the site, stock and tracking checked on the same day
forces.habit: wait a day to see if it settles
forces.anxiety: what if it is normal noise and I overreact

jobs.little_hire: any day spend or cost per purchase moves 50 percent against the last 14 days

watch.metric: hours from the jump to the cause found

drives.metric: spend lost to broken days, trailing 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a broken pixel is found 3 days late after $4,000 spent. After: found within 3 hours.
jobs.not_for: a store spending under $100 a day, where a bad day is a small loss

jobs.job: When the agency's monthly report says all is well and I cannot tell if it is true, check their calls against store profit, so I hold them to account instead of taking their word
